widgets_values:
WF 2a2 - SEEDVR2 COLMAP UPSCALE, ONE CAMERA VIEW AT A TIME

Same upscaler and same in-place result as 2a, but the dataset is STREAMED through
SeedVR2 in meta-batches instead of being loaded, upscaled and returned whole.

WHAT ACTUALLY BLEW UP IN 2a
Not SeedVR2's own VRAM -- its batch_size already capped that at 81 frames. The
killer was the ComfyUI tensors either side of it: 'Load Dataset Images (Ordered)'
returned all 1944 faces at once, and the node had to return every UPSCALED face in
one IMAGE batch before the saver ever ran. At resolution=2048 that return value
alone is 1944 x 2048 x 2048 x 3 x 4 bytes = ~98 GB. It cannot fit, whatever GPU
you have.

THE FIX
The Meta Batch Manager (frames_per_batch=81) makes ComfyUI re-run the whole rail
ONCE PER CAMERA VIEW. The loader yields 81 faces, SeedVR2 upscales those 81, the
streaming saver writes them to disk, and the tensors are freed before the next
iteration. Peak = one view, not the whole dataset. 1944 faces = 24 iterations.

WHY 81 AND NOT 1
SeedVR2 is a TEMPORAL model - a 1-frame meta-batch would destroy the very thing it
is good at. 81 is one full cube-face sub-video from the marker, so each iteration is
exactly one coherent view. Keep the three numbers in agreement:

    frames_per_batch (Meta Batch Manager)  ==  batch_size (SeedVR2)  ==  81

STILL OOMs? Step BOTH down together to a DIVISOR of the per-view length that is also
4n+1: 81 -> 9 -> 1. (27 and 3 divide 81 but are not 4n+1, so SeedVR2 would re-chunk
them.) Never pick 5/13/21 - they do not divide 81 and chunks would straddle two view
directions. The loader PRINTS a warning if frames_per_batch does not divide the
group size, and prints suggested_batch_size on every run.
The other lever is resolution (SeedVR2's target for the SHORT edge): on ~360px cube
faces 2048 is already a ~5.7x upscale. 1024 halves each edge and quarters the memory.

FRAME 00000 IS THE REAL PANORAMA - IT IS NOT UPSCALED
frame_00000's cube faces come from the ORIGINAL pano, so they are larger than the
rest (dark-alley-01: 512x512 vs 360x360) and COLMAP gives them their own camera --
cameras.bin here holds SIMPLE_PINHOLE 512x512 AND 360x360. They are real pixels; a
generative upscaler can only invent detail over them.

So on_size_mismatch=resize_and_passthrough does two things:
  LOAD  - the odd-sized faces are resized DOWN to the majority size, purely so the
          batch is uniform and SeedVR2 still gets them as temporal context.
  SAVE  - their generated output is DISCARDED. The untouched original file is copied
          byte-for-byte into images/ at its native 512x512.
That is what passthrough_json carries (loader -> saver): the folder plus the list of
names to copy rather than write. The console reports how many were passed through.
The mixed output size is CORRECT - each camera keeps matching its own images.

Set on_size_mismatch=error instead if you would rather be told about odd sizes than
have them handled - a corrupt reprojection looks identical to an original pano here.

ORDER MATTERS TWICE
1. Reading camera-major (all of face 0 across time, then face 1, ...) is what gives
   SeedVR2 a stable view per sequence, instead of the direction flipping 6x per frame.
2. Because of that, the arrival order is NOT lexical, so the saver is fed the
   loader's 'order_names' list - each upscaled face goes back to the filename it came
   from, and sparse/0/images.bin keeps matching. Do not swap this for a folder listing.

SAFETY / IDEMPOTENCE
'Prepare Dataset Upscale' does the images -> images_lowres rename ONCE, BEFORE the
loop, and recreates images/ empty. The swap cannot be done at the end the way 2a's
'Save Upscaled Dataset' does it: renaming the source folder mid-loop would make every
not-yet-read frame disappear. Re-running is safe - images_lowres/ already exists, so
nothing is renamed and images/ is simply refilled from the untouched originals.
Crashed half way? images/ is partial, originals are intact, just run it again.

HOW TO USE
1. Set 'dataset_name' on BOTH SplatKit nodes to your SphereSfM output_name.
   (The loader also takes load_dir on its dataset_path input, so it always reads the
   preserved originals rather than the folder being written.)
2. Queue ONCE. VHS requeues the graph itself, once per view; watch the console for
   'Meta-Batch n/24'.

The throwaway VHS_VideoCombine is REQUIRED: VideoHelperSuite only keeps a meta-batch
loop requeueing while a VHS_VideoCombine sits on the manager. It is fed the cheap
low-res frames with save_output=false, so it only advances the loop.

TOO SLOW / STILL TIGHT?

- camera_index on the loader (-1 = all) restricts the run to ONE view - one cube
  face within one trajectory. dark-alley-01 has 24 of them, 81 frames each, so you
  can time a single view before committing to the whole dataset.
- The console lists every camera_index and its frame range on each run.
- The loader probes every header up front, so a size problem shows up in seconds
  rather than an hour in. With resize_and_passthrough the odd frame-00000 faces are
  handled automatically (see the main note); with 'error' you get the file list.
- dark-alley-01 is currently MISSING 7 images that sparse/0/images.bin still
  registers (all six frame_00000 faces plus frame_00001_perspective_00000000).
  Restore them before running, or the passthrough has nothing to copy.
